draft.title: Diffusion
card: Diffusion is the spreading of particles from where there are many to where there are few. It happens because particles keep moving and bump into each other.
Diffusion carries on until the particles are spread out evenly. The particles do not stop moving when this happens.
Diffusion is faster in gases than in liquids. Gas particles are far apart and move freely, so they spread out more quickly.
Diffusion is faster when the substance is warmer. Warm particles move faster, so they spread sooner.
draft.remember: Moving particles spread out from crowded places to empty ones, and heat speeds this up.

a.q: A drop of food dye is placed in a glass of still water. Why does the colour slowly spread through the water?
opts: Dye particles keep moving and spread to where there are few
Dye particles stop moving and settle through the water
Water particles push the dye particles up towards the top
Dye particles melt into the water and become much smaller
a.why: Dye particles are always moving, so they spread from the crowded drop to places where there are few. The idea that particles stop is wrong, because they keep moving even after the colour looks even.
a.clue: Think about what particles are always doing.

b.q: Liam opens a bottle of perfume at one end of a room. Which change would make the smell reach the other end sooner?
opts: Warming the room, so the particles move faster
Cooling the room, so the particles move slower
Pouring the perfume onto the floor as a liquid
Closing the bottle so fewer particles escape
b.why: Warmer particles move faster, so diffusion is faster and the smell spreads sooner. Cooling the room does the opposite, because the particles move more slowly.
b.clue: What does heat do to the speed of particles?

a.best: Dye particles keep moving and spread to where there are few

b.best: Warming the room, so the particles move faster
also_right: Pouring the perfume onto the floor as a liquid

problems.detail: The distractor 'Pouring the perfume onto the floor as a liquid' can be defended as right. Spreading the liquid out gives a larger surface, so more perfume evaporates more quickly and the smell could reach the far end sooner. Replace it with a clearly wrong option.

'From crowded places to empty ones' is looser than the card's 'from where there are many to where there are few'. It suggests particles only spread into empty places. Use 'to places where there are fewer'.
